title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Thermal Expansion — 2024
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Define linear, superficial, and cubical expansivity. Derive the relationship between them.
questions.solution:
**Linear expansivity (α):** fractional change in length per kelvin, ΔL = αL₀ΔT.

**Superficial expansivity (β):** fractional change in area, ΔA = βA₀ΔT.

**Cubical expansivity (γ):** fractional change in volume, ΔV = γV₀ΔT.

Relation: each side L → L(1 + αΔT), so A → A(1 + αΔT)² ≈ A(1 + 2αΔT) and V → V(1 + αΔT)³ ≈ V(1 + 3αΔT). Hence **β = 2α and γ = 3α** for isotropic solids.
questions.knowledgeNote: For metals α ≈ 10⁻⁵–10⁻⁶ K⁻¹; steel α ≈ 11 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹.

questions.question: A steel rod 2 m long at 20°C is heated to 120°C. By how much does it expand? (α for steel = 12 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹)
questions.knowledgeNote: ΔT in °C equals ΔT in K — never add 273 when only a temperature *change* is needed.

questions.question: Why are small gaps left between consecutive rails of a railway track?
questions.solution:
In summer the rails expand (ΔL = αL₀ΔT). With no gap, the constrained expansion produces huge compressive stress that buckles the track sideways.

The gaps give each rail room to lengthen freely, so no thermal stress builds up.
questions.knowledgeNote: Same physics as sagging overhead power lines in summer and the rollers under bridge ends.

questions.question: A pendulum clock keeps correct time in winter but loses time in summer. Explain why.
questions.solution:
In summer the pendulum rod expands, so its length L increases. Period T = 2π√(L/g) grows with L.

Each swing takes slightly longer, so the clock ticks fewer times per hour — it **loses time**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Gridiron (compensation) pendulums pair high-α and low-α rods so the effective length stays constant.

questions.question: What is the anomalous expansion of water? Explain its importance for aquatic life in cold climates.
questions.solution:
Water **contracts** when heated from 0°C to 4°C and only expands above 4°C — so it is densest at **4°C**, the reverse of normal behaviour.

In a freezing lake, the 4°C water sinks to the bottom while 0°C ice floats on top. The ice sheet insulates the water below, which stays liquid at 4°C — so fish and plants survive winter under the ice.
questions.knowledgeNote: Hope's apparatus demonstrates this: water in the middle of the trough stays at 4°C while top and bottom freeze.

questions.question: What is a bimetallic strip? Explain its working with one application.
questions.solution:
A strip of two metals with different expansivities (e.g. brass and invar) bonded together. On heating, the high-α side lengthens more, so the strip **bends toward the low-α side**; it straightens on cooling.

**Application:** the thermostat in an electric iron — the bending strip breaks the heating circuit at the set temperature and remakes it as it cools.
questions.knowledgeNote: Bimetallic thermometers, fire alarms, and blinkers all use the same bend-with-temperature trick.
